See [the reusable kernel contract](kernel.md) for application ownership and the
non-research execution proof, and [installation boundaries](installations.md) for
independent records and runtime lifecycles. These remain inside this repository.

The local [improvement application](improvements.md) uses that same kernel contract
in an explicitly new experiment record. Captured public research informs code
proposals; it does not become writable research authority. Untrusted candidate
code runs only in restricted disposable containers, while the host scores its
outputs. An operator review receipt cannot apply code or grant release authority.

The [autonomous context lane](autonomous-context.md) is a separate WAKE application
policy on the existing per-node native authority. An installed capability permits
one selector-field change, gated by recomputed fixed-task and current-native-state
measurements. Proposal generation, adoption and rollback require no per-change
human review. Metadata events preserve research versions and history; candidate
data cannot replace the evaluator, widen permissions, modify code or create a
competing research store. Native replay owns the policy after restart.

> **Current specification.** This document explains why the present system is shaped this way: its trust boundary, durable record, governance model and known limits. Current local procedures belong in `standalone.md`; public mirror publishing belongs in `cloud.md`. Maintainer navigation, environment checks and reproducible validation guidance belong in `development.md`.

**WAKE✳︎** is infrastructure for continuity of accountable work, not continuity of a model instance. Its stable sequence is **Record → Context → Proposal → Governance → Transition → Receipt**. New to the project? Follow [the setup guide](setup.md) for local Docker, GitHub
Pages, VS Code and Codespaces, then return here for source and verification details.

Use [kernel development](kernel.md) for the application seam and
[multiple installations](installations.md) for parallel container operation.

This is the entry point for changing WAKE safely. The repository owns executable
behavior; installations own independent records. A shared source tree does not
imply a shared database, execution process, deployment, or provider quota ledger.
Read [architecture](architecture.md) for invariants, [mirror publishing](cloud.md)
for GitHub, and [standalone operation](standalone.md) for Docker.

Before changing anything, answer three questions:

1. **Which installation are you changing?** Local Docker and Codespace
   WAKE have separate records and processes.
2. **Which code is actually running there?** A checkout, mounted workspace and
   packaged image can all contain different versions.
3. **What are you authorized to change?** Editing, committing, pushing, restarting containers,
   uploading a public snapshot and resetting records are separate actions.

If you only need the key terms, use the [glossary](glossary.md). If you need a
release procedure, go to [mirror publishing](cloud.md#development-and-release).

Long verification and delivery jobs should run in the background while independent
authorized work continues. Check completion only when reaching its next dependent
publication or runtime operation. Do not repeatedly poll an unchanged job or
rerun unaffected suites to fill the wait. Use the release boundaries in
[hosted upgrades](cloud.md#publish-source-without-upgrading-records) to choose checks;
full history replay is a record-compatibility gate, not a universal UI gate.
